targets.authors: Ihme, T. A., and Tausendpfund, M.
targets.title: Gender Differences in Political Knowledge: Bringing Situation Back In
targets.evidence_quote: As part of the Systematizing Confidence in Open Research and Evidence (SCORE) program, we conducted a two-stage preregistered and high-powered direct replication of Study 2 of Ihme and Tausendpfund (2018).
targets.outcome_quote: Thus, according to the criteria outlined by SCORE, the replication of the effect of stereotype threat on the gender gap on political knowledge was unsuccessful even after the second stage of data collection.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly judge the focal stereotype-threat replication unsuccessful after both stages. The successful gender main effect is an ancillary comparison; it does not overturn their overall verdict on the focal replication.

reasoning: Full article and references identify one target paper. The two data-collection stages are aggregated. Analysis of original data for scale difficulty is ancillary to the new-sample replication.
